spec.title: voice-lint: scope the voice obligation to the turn that produced the record
spec.problem: voice-lint.mjs decides whether to impose voice.md's shape from one input: the current_phase of whichever .pipeline/<issue>/status.json is newest by mtime. Phase alone carries no notion of WHEN, and no notion of WHOSE. Two failures follow, and both were reproduced at HEAD (587a4aa) with a proper hook fixture. (a) IN-RUN: 5-archived is terminal, so once a run archives, every later message in that session is graded as the completion report. The issue records three consecutive instances and this session's orchestrator hit the same class again. (b) CROSS-RUN, sharper than #56 describes: when the current run's record is REMOVED at archival, resolveStatus falls through to the next-newest status.json, which is some other lane's parked record, and grades this session's message against a run this session does not own. That is exactly what happened here: .pipeline/53/status.json was removed at a1634d9 around 13:20 local, which made .pipeline/40/status.json (mtime 2026-08-22 08:23:08, current_phase 4-review-complete, branch claude/lane-4-a521bf) the strict newest until .pipeline/56 was written at 13:52:52, and a message in that window was refused for missing the panel-result scales. THE RULING ON THE THREE OPTIONS FOLLOWS FROM (b). Option 2 (clear the record on archival) is not merely out of lane, it is REFUTED: removal is the direct cause of the cross-run capture, so the issue's recommended fix converts an in-run false positive into a cross-run one. Option 1 (a voice_report_at / events[] delivery marker) is blocked by ownership: the writer would be commands/pipeline.md, which this lane may not touch, and it leaves the cross-run half open regardless, because a marker cannot be written into a record this session never had. So the fix is option 3, and the issue's objection to it ('it pushes state into a stateless check') dissolves once the state is not remembered but DERIVED: the Stop payload already names the transcript, and the transcript already carries the turn boundary. The sibling control in this same lane settled the same question the same way and says so in its own header (gate-phase-entry.mjs's in-flight predicate); voice-lint is the sibling with no recency ceiling at all. WHAT THE PHASE-2 ROUND-1 REVIEW CHANGED, and this is the whole of the rework: the DESIGN survived every reviewer (SecOps: 'the direction is right'; DBA: 'the design is right and the ruling against options 1 and 2 is well-evidenced'), but the MECHANISM did not. The round-1 R5 defined a human turn by EXCLUDING two spellings the vendor owns, which is the wrong side of the transformation, and it therefore admitted the harness's own records as human turns: voice-lint's OWN blocking refusal (so the control disarmed itself on first fire), background task-completion notices, auto-compaction continuations, and cross-session messages from another process on the same machine. R5 is now stated as POSITIVE provenance identification and the measurements below are re-derived at a wider grain than round 1 used.
spec.root_cause: run() derives the obligation from current_phase and nothing else. current_phase records that a run REACHED a state, never that the state is still the subject of the turn now ending, and never that this session owns it. A terminal phase therefore states a true fact forever, and the mtime fallback lends that fact to whoever stops next in the project. The SECOND root cause, surfaced by Phase 2 and now fixed in this spec rather than in the diff: a freshness predicate that decides 'has a person weighed in' by subtracting known machine spellings from the set of user records inherits every future spelling the vendor adds, and each of those is a silent disarm of a blocking control.
requirements: R1. voice-lint imposes the voice shape only when the resolved status record was written DURING the turn now ending. Stated as an outcome property, not a mechanism: after the change, no message can be refused on account of a record that has not been touched since the last OWNER-AUTHORED turn began. The predicate is phase-independent, so 5-archived, halted-error and the <phase>-error family all inherit it.

R2. The predicate is applied AFTER resolution and to BOTH resolution branches (the CLAUDE_PIPELINE_ACTIVE_ISSUE signal and the newest-mtime fallback). An explicit signal must not be able to re-open the in-run false positive. Measured at this checkout: 0 files under plugins/ assign that variable outside tests/, out of 32 grep hits under plugins/, so the fallback is the live path today, but the branch must not become a second behaviour.

R3. FAIL DIRECTION, and this is the load-bearing half. Stated over the CLASSIFICATION, not only over the timestamp, because that is where round 1 was falsified: an UNRECOGNISED record shape is NOT a human turn. That leaves the boundary earlier, which leaves the lint louder. Any transcript that yields no human turn at all (no record positively identifiable as owner-authored, absent or unparseable timestamp, unreadable or unparseable transcript, a record shape the predicate does not recognise) leaves behaviour EXACTLY AS IT IS TODAY. THE OUTCOME PROPERTY IS 'EXACTLY AS TODAY'; ROUND 2 RESTATED IT AS 'THE LINT FIRES', WHICH IS TRUE OF THREE OF THOSE FOUR INPUTS AND FALSE OF THE FOURTH, AND THAT IS THE CONTRADICTION AC7 INHERITED. Corrected and stated as the property that actually governs: THIS CHANGE MUST NEVER BE THE REASON FOR SILENCE - an unresolvable boundary never suppresses a refusal today's code would have produced. For the three inputs where today's code produces a refusal (no owner-authored record, absent or unparseable timestamp, an unrecognised record shape) that means the lint fires. FOR AN UNREADABLE OR WHOLLY UNPARSEABLE TRANSCRIPT, TODAY'S BEHAVIOUR IS ALREADY SILENCE (rc 0), AND THIS SPEC PRESERVES IT DELIBERATELY, AS PRESERVATION AND NOT AS A CHANGE: lastAssistantText catches the read failure and returns the empty string (voice-lint.mjs:192-199), and run() then returns no failures at the `if (text.trim() === '') return { failures: [], phase }` line, which sits BEFORE any boundary question and is untouched by this change. There is no message to grade, so there is nothing to refuse. Making that input exit 2 would be a NEW false-refusal class fired by a malformed hook payload, would contradict R6's unchanged process contract, and would refuse on an input carrying no voice content at all. VERIFIED LIVE AT ROUND 3 THROUGH THE REAL CLI, with a FRESH record so the record is not the reason for silence, and with a non-zero control on the same project dir: transcript_path absent -> rc 0; transcript_path present at mode 000 -> rc 0; the identical dir with a readable-but-defective transcript -> rc 2. Re-confirmed identically against an R5/R9 reference predicate, so the new boundary predicate does not change it either. The distinction that makes both halves consistent: silence must never be the product of a tooling failure IN THE NEW PREDICATE, or of a vendor change to the transcript record shape, because a silently disarmed voice check is the same defect class this issue is about, one size up; the pre-existing no-assistant-text-no-lint path is a different thing, it predates #56, and this spec neither widens nor narrows it. MEASURED over a 10-class drift battery x 6 behavioural cells: the round-1 predicate went SILENT in every drift row; the predicate in R5 below is LOUD in all 10 (see measured_state, 'vendor-drift battery').

R4. resolveStatus's precedence and tie rule (explicit signal, then STRICT newest mtime, then null on a tie) are unchanged. WORDING CORRECTED FROM ROUND 1, which claimed it 'keeps mirroring validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs's activeIssueDir': the two mirror on the newest-mtime FALLBACK branch and DIVERGE on the named-signal branch, measured live at HEAD on three inputs (see AC9). R4 freezes voice-lint's CURRENT behaviour and asks for no behaviour change; what it drops is the false claim of a mirror that the divergence table now replaces. If run() needs the resolved record's path or mtime, that is added as a returned value, never by reordering or re-scoping the resolution. Verified safe: resolveStatus has no importer outside voice-lint.mjs.

R5. A HUMAN TURN IS IDENTIFIED POSITIVELY, NEVER BY EXCLUSION. This requirement replaces round 1's R5 in full and is the fix for the SecOps veto and for DBA's second blocker. OUTCOME PROPERTY FIRST: a transcript record the OWNER did not type must not advance the turn boundary, and where a record's provenance cannot be POSITIVELY established the boundary does NOT advance, which keeps the lint loud per R3. MECHANISM, measured rather than reasoned: a record is a human turn when ALL of these are positively true - type === 'user'; isSidechain !== true; isMeta !== true; message.role === 'user'; origin.kind === 'human'; and timestamp is a string Date.parse yields a finite value for. Everything else is not a human turn. WHERE `origin` LIVES, STATED PLAINLY BECAUSE THE CLAUSE ORDER ABOVE READS AMBIGUOUSLY AND THE MISREADING IS FATAL: `origin` IS A RECORD-LEVEL OBJECT, a sibling of type, isSidechain, isMeta, timestamp AND message. It is NOT message.origin. The access is record.origin?.kind, NEVER record.message?.origin?.kind. Measured at round 3 over the whole corpus, 1,817 transcript files and 398,088 records (main-session and subagent): 2,742 RECORD-level origin objects (2,391 main + 351 subagent) and ZERO under message, anywhere, in any client version. THE COST OF GETTING THIS WRONG IS THE WORST OUTCOME IN THIS SPEC, which is why it is spelled out rather than left to the clause order: an implementer who nests it under message - the natural misreading, because origin.kind is listed immediately after message.role and shares its rhythm - finds ZERO human turns on every transcript ever written, R3's fallback fires every time, and the change ships as a PERMANENT, TOTAL, SILENT no-op that looks exactly like the control working. It is byte-for-byte the same failure class as the Array.isArray(content) mistake AC15 exists to catch. AC14's drift battery CANNOT catch it, because a permanently-loud predicate passes every drift cell trivially - loud is what those cells assert. AC8's nesting-discrimination pair is what catches it. THE PREDICATE READS NO MESSAGE CONTENT AT ALL, and that is a ruling: reading content is what produced two of SecOps's three SILENT drift classes (a renamed tool_result block type, tool results relocated out of message.content[]) and their string-vs-array concern, and dropping the content read removes both at once. It also stops the predicate rejecting the 12 measured owner messages whose content is an array carrying an image block. WHY origin.kind: measured over 84 transcripts and 134,438 records, it is the vendor's own provenance label and it discriminates the classes that defeated round 1 completely - 1377 of 1377 background task-completion records carry origin.kind 'task-notification' and none carries an absent origin; 31 of 31 cross-session messages carry origin.kind 'peer'; voice-lint's own refusal records and auto-compaction summaries carry no origin at all. isMeta and isSidechain are KEPT even though origin.kind alone would exclude every observed instance, because they cost nothing, they only ever narrow (narrower is louder is safer), and they give the cross-session class a SECOND independent exclusion; see R7 residual (v).

R6. The process contract to hooks/stop.sh is unchanged: exit 0 is silent, exit 2 blocks and carries the named failures, the voice.md pointer and the CLAUDE_HOOK_STOP_SKIP=1 line. hooks/stop.sh is not edited. SPELLED OUT AT ROUND 3, because round 2's AC7 contradicted this requirement without either side noticing: NO INPUT ACQUIRES A NEW EXIT-2 THAT IT DOES NOT HAVE TODAY. This spec only ever REMOVES refusals (the stale-record ones), never adds a refusal class. In particular an unreadable or wholly unparseable transcript exits 0 today and still exits 0 after this change - see R3 and AC7's corrected cell - because there is no assistant text to grade; a malformed hook payload must not be able to make this hook block.

R7. The module header records the residual limits, each with its FAIL DIRECTION and its expiry condition, in the style the file already uses. Round 1 stated the first one backwards and that sentence was slated to ship verbatim into the header and the knowledge store; it is corrected here. (i) A mid-turn operation that rewrites a foreign status.json's mtime (a git checkout, clone, worktree add or sync) can make that record look fresh and capture the turn. THIS FAILS TOWARD A FALSE REFUSAL, not toward silence: the lint fires against a record the session does not own, which is exactly today's behaviour and is failure (b) of this spec's own problem statement. The header records WHY the sibling module's tie-abstention does not cover it: measured on this APFS worktree, four bulk-written records share one wall-clock second (epoch 1787232363) and differ only at sub-millisecond resolution across a ~2 ms spread, so resolveStatus picks a strict winner rather than abstaining. (ii) If the owner sends a message between the archive checkpoint and the completion report, the report is no longer in the same turn and the genuine moment goes unchecked. THIS FAILS TOWARD SILENCE and is the one true positive the fix trades away; it is q3's accepted cost. (iii) THE REVERSE OF (i). ROUND 2 TREATED THIS AS ONE RESIDUAL AND IT IS TWO, WITH DIFFERENT ANSWERS; conflating them is what let round 2 certify as CLOSED a class that is still open, in a sentence R9 mandates shipping verbatim into the module header and the knowledge store. Both halves fail toward SILENCE. (iii-a) BOUNDED BY R9: the BYTES were freshly written this turn and only the timestamp moved backwards (an NTP step backwards, an explicit utimes). Such a record still carries a recent updated_at, so max(mtimeMs, Date.parse(updated_at)) reads fresh and the lint fires. This is the half max() actually bounds, and it is the half round 2 mentioned last and named no tool for. (iii-b) OPEN, AND BOUNDED BY NOTHING THIS SPEC SHIPS: an mtime-PRESERVING RESTORE (cp -p, rsync -a, tar -x). updated_at is file CONTENT, so a verbatim copy carries the OLD updated_at along with the OLD mtime, BOTH terms of the max() are stale together, and the composition reads the record as old even though it was placed in this very turn. RE-DERIVED INDEPENDENTLY AT ROUND 3 rather than taken from the review: a record whose mtime and updated_at are both 72h old, placed at 2026-08-22T21:41:10Z, reads max(mtime, updated_at) = 72.00 hours stale after cp -p, after tar -x, AND after rsync -a (which the round-2 review listed as untested); the non-preserving control, a plain cp of the identical source, reads 0.00 hours. Behaviourally through the real module with an R5/R9 reference predicate: the restore signature exits 0 (SILENT) while the same fixture with only the mtime moved forward exits 2. DIRECTION: SILENCE, a missed check. EXPIRY: a mechanism that dates the record by something a verbatim copy cannot carry. ctime WAS CONSIDERED AND IS REJECTED WITH ITS MEASUREMENT, so it is not re-proposed cold: ctime is set by the copy and cannot be preserved by any userspace call, so max(mtimeMs, updated_at, ctimeMs) does read 0.00h fresh on all three restores - but ctime is set by ANY inode change, including the utimesSync that R8 mandates as the only sanctioned way to stale a fixture. Measured: a file stamped to T-72h with utimesSync carries mtime 72.00h old and ctime 0.00h old, so under a ctime-inclusive composition a utimesSync-stamped fixture reads FRESH and every stale-record cell in this spec (AC1, AC2, AC3, AC10, AC16) would stop meaning what it says. THE REASON IS THE FIXTURE COST, NOT IMPOSSIBILITY, AND AN EARLIER DRAFT OF THIS SENTENCE OVERSTATED IT: it claimed such a fixture 'cannot be built at all', and that is FALSE. Re-measured, the counter-method works - write status.json, let real wall-clock time elapse, and only then take the turn boundary, and the file's mtime and ctime land on the same value and read STALE under BOTH compositions, with a fresh control on the same method reading fresh under both, so the composition still discriminates. THE ACTUAL OBJECTION, which is the one that ships: a ctime-inclusive composition would force every fixture needing a stale timestamp to become TIMING-DEPENDENT (a real sleep, measured at 1.1s per fixture here) instead of instantly and deterministically stamped, because nothing in userspace moves ctime backwards. That trades R8's deterministic utimesSync idiom - chosen precisely to keep these cells fast and reproducible across a BSD author machine and a GNU CI runner - for a slower, flakier, wall-clock-dependent suite, multiplied across every stale cell in AC1/AC2/AC3/AC10/AC16. Paying that on every run to close a residual with zero observed occurrences is the wrong trade. The RULING is unchanged; only its stated reason is corrected, and it is corrected here because R9 mandates this reasoning ship into the module header and the knowledge store, where a wrong reason outlives the person who wrote it. FREQUENCY, upgraded from round 2's 'nobody has measured' to a measured zero WITH ITS BOUNDARY STATED: zero occurrences of cp -p, rsync, or tar -x anywhere under plugins/ or .github/ at this checkout; the only timestamp writes in the entire plugin are three utimesSync calls in validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs's own test fixtures (:942, :1075, :1171), which are (iii-a)'s shape and not (iii-b)'s. That measurement bounds what THIS REPO does and nothing else. The restore event occurs in an OPERATOR'S SHELL - a backup restore, a worktree sync tool, an unarchived tree - which is an environment no check in this repo runs in, so no test here can witness the real event and the residual is DECLARED rather than closed. AC16(d) pins its behaviour anyway. (vii) A TURN THAT THE OWNER DID NOT START DOES NOT ADVANCE THE BOUNDARY, SO THE ARCHIVED RECORD IS STILL FRESH RELATIVE TO IT AND THAT TURN'S MESSAGE IS STILL GRADED AS THE COMPLETION REPORT. This is the honest other side of R5's positive identification, and round 2 booked only one side of the trade. Under R5 the boundary advances ONLY on an owner-TYPED record, so when the next turn is initiated by anything else - an auto-compaction continuation, a background task-completion notice handing control back, a queued or scheduled message firing, a session resume, a cross-session peer message - the boundary stays where it was, a status record written after that boundary still reads fresh, and the message gets voice-graded even though no person has read anything since. DIRECTION: FALSE REFUSAL, i.e. exactly today's behaviour. This is a COVERAGE LIMIT, not a regression: the fix simply does not help in these turns, it does not make them worse. Round 1's predicate DID advance the boundary on these records, and giving that up is what closes the self-disarm (AC13), so this is a deliberate trade and not an oversight. VERIFIED BEHAVIOURALLY AT ROUND 3, not reasoned: with an owner record at T-60m, a status write at T-30m and a non-owner initiator at T-10m, a task-notification initiator, an auto-compaction continuation and a cross-session peer initiator each produce rc 2, while the DISCRIMINATING CONTROL - an owner-typed record in the same position - produces rc 0. THE BOUND, which is tighter than 'problem (a) is live' and is the part DBA's framing understates: the residual only bites in the WINDOW between a status write and the NEXT owner-typed message, because the next owner message moves the boundary past the record and silences it permanently. So it is the in-run half of problem (a) restricted to that window, not the whole of problem (a). MEASURED FREQUENCY, with its grain stated because two grains disagree here and only one answers the question: over the 85 main-session transcripts, of 15,003 assistant TEXT records with a resolvable preceding turn-initiator, 8,610 (57.4%) sit in a turn an owner started and 6,393 (42.6%) do not; counted as EPISODES instead (consecutive assistant texts under one initiator collapsed to one, which is the closer proxy for a turn), 961 of 2,572 (37.4%) are owner-started and 1,611 (62.6%) are not. Excluding voice-lint's OWN refusal records, which continue the owner's turn rather than beginning a new one and must not be counted as a residual, the non-owner-started figure is 6,204 records / 1,562 episodes (41.4% / 60.7%). Initiator classes behind those episodes: task-notification 1,364, other isMeta without an origin 123, cross-session peer 31, auto-compaction continuation 22, no-origin-not-meta 22. THAT IS A POPULATION, NOT A FALSE-REFUSAL RATE: the residual only fires where such a turn also follows a voice-moment status write inside the window above, and this corpus carries no status.json history to join against, so the rate itself is unmeasured and the header says so. EXPIRY: a structural signal for 'a new turn began' that is independent of authorship, at which point the boundary can advance on turn starts rather than on owner messages and this residual closes without reopening AC13. (iv) THE IRREDUCIBLE ONE, and the honest cost of positive identification: the predicate TRUSTS THE VENDOR'S OWN PROVENANCE LABEL. If the client ever stamps a harness-injected record origin.kind 'human', that record advances the boundary and the control goes silent, with no error anywhere. This is the one drift class the battery cannot survive and it is recorded as the declared expected survivor rather than papered over. Expiry: re-run the origin.kind census over a fresh transcript corpus and check that no non-owner class carries 'human'. (v) A same-machine cross-session message is EXCLUDED TWICE OVER, not bounded as a residual, and the header states both exclusions so a reader can see the depth: measured, all 31 observed cross-session records carry BOTH origin.kind 'peer' AND isMeta true. sessionId is NOT a third guard and the header says so with the measurement, so a future reader does not re-propose it cold: all 31 are stamped with the RECEIVING session's own id, so a sessionId equality test cannot see them. (vi) On client versions that predate the origin field the predicate finds no human turn, so the boundary is unresolvable and the lint fires unconditionally, which is today's behaviour. Measured: 8 of 84 transcripts (9.5%) contain no origin.kind 'human' record at all, all on clients 2.1.170 and older; on clients 2.1.209 and newer the predicate catches 968 of 968 owner records. The fix is a LOUD no-op there, not a disarm. R10 is what makes that condition visible instead of invisible.

R8. New test cells are built from synthetic fixtures written by the suite, seeded where possible with records CAPTURED from a live transcript rather than hand-written (a hand-copied fixture restates the contract instead of observing it). No population is derived from a git range against a moving ref, from committed .pipeline history, or from the live .pipeline directory (#37/#68). FILE MTIMES ARE SET WITH node fs.utimesSync, NAMED RATHER THAN LEFT OPEN, because round 1 banned `touch -t` without naming a spelling that exists on both runners: BSD touch on macOS (the author's machine) has no `-d @<epoch>` form, GNU touch on ubuntu-latest (CI, .github/workflows/tests.yml) does, so a Dev reaching for the obvious bash idiom writes a test that passes in CI and fails on the reviewer's machine. The in-tree idiom to copy is `utimesSync(file, ms / 1000, ms / 1000)` at validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs:1075 and :1171 (a third at :942). The only existing mtime fixture in the test tree, test-gate-phase-entry.sh:824-825, uses the `touch -t` form this rule forbids, so there is no in-suite precedent to copy. `touch -t` is banned for a second reason round 1 measured: it takes a LOCAL-clock value while transcript timestamps are UTC ISO, so a fixture mixing the two measures the runner's timezone (`touch -t 202608221341` produced a 17:41Z mtime on this machine, which is UTC-4). AND THE SUITE ASSERTS THE STAMP IT APPLIED: after stamping, read the mtime back and assert it lands within a stated tolerance of the intended epoch value, so a stamp that silently no-ops is named where it happened instead of leaving the record at 'now' and reddening a distant cell for the wrong reason.

R9. THE RULING ON updated_at, which round 1 never mentioned and which is a third input already sitting in the schema. status.schema.json lists `updated_at` in `required` alongside current_phase, typed string/date-time, in the SAME UTC ISO grain as the transcript timestamps, and all 9 live records carry it. The sibling control made the OPPOSITE choice deliberately for the analogous question (gate-phase-entry.mjs's inFlight dates a record from its own updated_at and abstains when that will not parse), so the absence of a ruling here is a gap a future reader will re-propose cold. RULED: mtime remains the primary reference and updated_at may only WIDEN freshness, never narrow it. Concretely, recordMs = max(mtimeMs, Date.parse(updated_at) where that is finite); an absent, non-string or unparseable updated_at contributes nothing and can never poison the comparison. THE MEASURED BASIS: mtime is the record's write time exactly when nothing has touched the file since, and a checkout timestamp otherwise - across the 9 live records the three written in place by the orchestrator agree with updated_at to under a second (34: 0.370s, 43: 0.233s) while six disagree by 3.0 hours to 13.7 days (21: 10,765.7s; 39: 47,128.6s; 17: 119,433.5s; exp-script-test-coverage: 1,182,075.5s), because their mtime is a git-checkout artifact. And updated_at cannot be trusted alone: measured, `updated_at` appears ONCE in commands/pipeline.md against 33 occurrences of `current_phase`, so its refresh is a writer convention restated at 1 of 33 write sites, and preferring it would trade a loud failure for a silent one. DIRECTION IS THE WHOLE ARGUMENT, AND IT IS AN ARGUMENT FOR KEEPING max(), NOT FOR WHAT ROUND 2 CLAIMED max() ACHIEVES: it is monotone in the loud direction, so it can only ever cause the lint to fire where it would otherwise have gone silent. That is why the mechanism stands unchanged at round 3. WHAT IT BOUNDS AND WHAT IT DOES NOT, STATED IN ONE SENTENCE SO THE HEADER CANNOT SHIP THE HALF-TRUTH AGAIN: max() bounds an mtime moved backwards while the BYTES were freshly written (R7 iii-a: an NTP step backwards, an explicit utimes, where a record written this turn still carries a recent updated_at), and it does NOT bound an mtime-PRESERVING RESTORE (R7 iii-b: cp -p, rsync -a, tar -x), because updated_at is file CONTENT and is restored along with the stale mtime, leaving both terms stale together. Measured at round 3: a cp -p, a tar -x and an rsync -a performed today on a 72-hour-old record each leave max(mtime, updated_at) reading 72.00 hours stale. ROUND 2 SAID max() 'CLOSES (iii)' IN FOUR PLACES AND IT DOES NOT; that claim is withdrawn here, in R7(iii), in AC16(a)'s label and in falsifiability_pass.unmutable, because R9 mandates this sentence be copied into the module header and the knowledge store and a false claim there is round 1's R7(i) defect rebuilt. AND THE WIDENING TERM HAS NO OBSERVED INPUT, recorded so a future reader knows this is forward-looking defence rather than a fix for something seen: across all 9 live records ZERO have updated_at LATER than mtime - every one runs in the mtime-later direction, deltas 0.2s to 13.7 days - so the max() term never fires on any record that currently exists, and AC16(a) is the only place its behaviour is observable at all. The ruling and its basis go in the module header beside the residuals, in the idiom the file already uses for the tables it declines to freeze.

R10. THE UNRESOLVABLE-BOUNDARY FALLBACK IS VISIBLE TO THE OPERATOR. R3's fail direction is loud, and a loud failure is a nuisance nobody reports as a bug, so a fix that has silently degraded to a permanent no-op (R7 vi, or any future vendor change) looks exactly like the control working. When the lint refuses AND no human turn was resolvable, the refusal text carries one additional fixed line saying so, in plain language, so the no-op condition is named at the moment output already happens and costs nothing when it does not apply. The line is a FIXED LITERAL: no byte of the transcript may appear in it, per the standing rule that nothing from the transcript reaches stderr.

R11. THE HUMAN-TURN SCAN MUST NOT REACH main()'s OUTER CATCH. main() wraps run() in a blanket try/catch that exits 0 on any uncaught exception (voice-lint.mjs:314-319), which is fail-OPEN and therefore the exact opposite of R3's direction; the sibling module shipped precisely this defect at #61, graded there as the most serious thing in that review. The scan uses the same per-field defensive idiom lastAssistantText already uses: optional chaining on every field access it makes, a per-record guard that treats a malformed record as NOT a human turn rather than throwing, and no assumption that a parsed JSON line is even an object. PHRASING CORRECTED AT ROUND 3: round 2 wrote 'optional chaining on every record/message/origin access' as though record, message and origin were three peers, which fed exactly the nesting ambiguity R5 now closes. The accesses are record.type, record.isSidechain, record.isMeta, record.timestamp, record.message?.role and record.origin?.kind - `message` and `origin` are BOTH direct children of the record and are NOT nested in one another. Guard each of those six, at the level it actually occurs. R11 is what makes R3 hold against the open-ended tail of unusual-but-parseable record shapes rather than only against the four inputs AC7 names.

R12. THE TRANSCRIPT IS READ ONCE PER STOP INVOCATION. lastAssistantText already does a full read + split + reverse JSON.parse; a second identical pass for the boundary doubles a cost measured at 620 ms on the largest transcript on this machine (69.8 MB, 26,460 records), and a Stop hook slow enough to be timed out by the harness is a silent disarm in the same direction as everything else in this review. Both derived values come out of one pass, or the header records why two passes are acceptable with the measured cost.
acceptance_criteria: AC1. CROSS-RUN, silenced. A project holding only a foreign lane's record at 4-review-complete, mtime and updated_at BOTH before the last human turn, and a last assistant message carrying none of the scales: exit 0 and ZERO bytes on stderr. (Reproduced red at 587a4aa: rc 2, stderr naming 4-review-complete and two missing scales.) THE OWNER-AUTHORED RECORD THAT ESTABLISHES THE BOUNDARY IN THIS CELL IS CAPTURED FROM A LIVE TRANSCRIPT, NOT HAND-WRITTEN, with its RECORD-LEVEL origin.kind 'human' asserted as a pinned present-tense fact (added at round 3): this cell only silences if the predicate actually resolves a boundary, so a hand-written owner record carrying `origin` at the wrong nesting level would make the cell pass for the wrong reason under an implementation that reads it at that same wrong level. See R5 and AC8(f).

AC2. NON-ZERO CONTROL for AC1, one variable moved. The identical project, identical transcript, identical message, with that same record's mtime moved to AFTER the last human turn: exit 2, stderr naming 4-review-complete. (d) NEW AT ROUND 3, THE DECLARED OPEN RESIDUAL R7(iii-b), pinned as a cell in the same residual-limit idiom R7(i) already uses, so the trade lives in the test output and not only in the module header: the RESTORE SIGNATURE - mtime STALE and updated_at STALE together - exits 0, and the cell is LABELLED with its DIRECTION (SILENCE, a missed check, not a false refusal) and its EXPIRY WRITTEN INTO THE ASSERTION MESSAGE: if this cell ever exits 2, either a mechanism now dates the record by something a verbatim copy cannot carry, or the fixture no longer constructs the restore signature, and this cell needs a new subject or deletion. ASSERTED AS A PAIR, moving ONE variable: the identical fixture with the mtime moved FORWARD exits 2, so cell (d)'s silence is genuine and not a lint that stopped firing for an unrelated reason. THE SIGNATURE IS BUILT WITH utimesSync PLUS A STALE updated_at WRITTEN INTO THE CONTENT, never by shelling out to cp -p, rsync or tar: that pair IS the restore's whole observable signature, and shelling out would reintroduce exactly R8's ban on touch -t in another costume (rsync is not verified present on the ubuntu-latest runner, and BSD and GNU cp differ). Measured at round 3, boundary at T-1h, stale at T-72h, fresh at T-30m: (a) rc 2, (b) rc 2, (c) rc 2 with a fresh mtime and rc 0 with a stale one (tracking mtime alone, as specified), (d) rc 0, (d)-control rc 2.

concerns.description: R7(iii-b)'s REJECTION OF ctime STATES A REASON THAT IS FALSE, IN A SENTENCE R7 MANDATES SHIPPING VERBATIM INTO THE MODULE HEADER. The premise is measured correctly and I reproduced it -- a file stamped to T-72h with utimesSync carries mtime 72.00h and ctime 0.00h -- but the CONCLUSION does not follow, because utimesSync is not the only way to build a stale fixture. MEASURED, run just now with NO utimesSync anywhere: write status.json, let 1.1 s of real time elapse, then stamp the owner transcript record with a timestamp taken after the write. The file carries mtime == ctime EXACTLY (delta 0.000 ms), and the record reads STALE under BOTH compositions -- boundary minus max(mtime, updated_at) = 1100 ms, boundary minus max(mtime, updated_at, ctime) = 1100 ms -- and the paired FRESH control (record written after the boundary) builds the same way. So the stale fixtures ARE buildable under a ctime-inclusive composition; what changes is the technique. The true objection is a real one and BA did not state it: adopting ctime would require rebuilding every stale cell by write-ordering against real elapsed time, trading a deterministic stamped fixture for a timing-dependent one, which is a flake surface and cuts against R8's own portability reasoning. THE RULING SURVIVES; the stated reason does not. This is the third round in which a residual's disposition is overstated in the sentence R7 sends to the header and the knowledge store, and it is why I am naming it rather than letting it pass: a future reader is told ctime is IMPOSSIBLE when it is merely costly, and will not revisit the one mechanism measured to close (iii-b) (ctime reads 0.00h fresh after cp -p, tar -x and rsync -a alike, and it is monotone in the loud direction exactly as updated_at is). concerns.description: AC8's SURVIVOR LIST IS OVER-BROAD BY ONE CLAUSE, AND THE MISSING ASSERTION IS FREE. AC8's falsifiability entry declares isSidechain, isMeta and message.role all as expected survivors, on the correct ground that 0 records co-occur origin.kind 'human' with any of them, so a clause-drop cannot redden a CAPTURED fixture. I reproduced that: 0 co-occurrences in all four combinations across 399,019 records, and dropping isMeta against captured fixtures reddens nothing (2 -> 2 on all four classes). BUT the entry evaluates the clause-drop against ONE fixture family. Run the cross product with AC14's ALREADY-SPECIFIED relabel fixtures and isMeta becomes falsifiable: dropping isMeta flips the Stop-hook refusal cell from 2 to 0 and the cross-session peer cell from 2 to 0, while dropping isSidechain flips nothing anywhere. This is this spec's own compound-predicate rule turned on the spec: a battery can only mutate the code its fixtures reach, so naming the fixture MATRIX over the cross product is the thing that separates a real survivor from an unexercised one. isSidechain and message.role are genuine survivors and should stay declared as such. isMeta is not, and promoting it costs one cell that the spec already builds. IMPORTANTLY THIS DOES NOT REQUIRE FABRICATING ANYTHING: the relabelled record is AC14's drift fixture, not a manufactured collision, so BA's explicit ban on fabricating origin.kind 'human' + isMeta true to force a red is untouched and I endorse it.

AC7's own mutation entry (make an unresolvable boundary CONTRIBUTE a failure rather than attach a line to an existing refusal) is the right mutation and it is the exact over-reading that produced round 2's error.

R7(iii-b) IS ACCEPTABLE AS A DECLARED RESIDUAL AND SHOULD NOT BLOCK. I re-derived it end to end rather than accepting DBA's or BA's account. A status.json stamped to T-72h in both its mtime and its content updated_at, copied today: cp -p reads max(mtime, updated_at) 72.00h stale, tar -x 72.00h, rsync -a 72.00h, and the non-preserving control (plain cp) reads 0.00h. So max() genuinely does not bound the restore class and round 2's 'closes (iii)' was wrong in four places, correctly withdrawn. THREE REASONS IT DOES NOT NEED TO BLOCK, in my own terms. (1) ENVIRONMENT: the event occurs in an operator's shell restoring a tree, which is an environment no check in this repo runs in, so no test here can witness it; a control has to be a mechanism, not an assertion. (2) THE ONLY MECHANISM REFUSES TOO MUCH: ctime does close it (0.00h fresh after all three restores, measured) but utimesSync leaves ctime at 0.00h too, so a ctime-inclusive composition reads every deliberately-stale fixture as FRESH and AC1/AC2/AC3/AC10/AC16 become unbuildable. Asking what the proposed control REFUSES is the right test and BA ran it. (3) DIRECTION AND BLAST RADIUS: the worst case is one voice-moment message going unshape-checked. It cannot make the system claim more than it knows, it touches no auth, data or compliance path, and the triggering tools appear 0 times under plugins/ and .github/ at this checkout (re-derived). The alternative to declaring it is holding the fix, which keeps three false refusals per run live indefinitely. It is written down properly: R7(iii-b) with its direction, R9's corrected sentence, and AC16(d) as a labelled cell with its expiry in the assertion message and a one-variable control. ONE SUGGESTION, not a change request: AC16(d)'s expiry message should also name the ENVIRONMENT (an operator shell), so a future reader does not try to close it with a CI test and conclude from a green run that it is closed.

R7(vii) IS THE ACCEPTABLE KIND OF RESIDUAL AND I VERIFIED ITS DIRECTION RATHER THAN TAKING IT. With an owner record at T-60m, a status write at T-30m and a non-owner turn-initiator after it, all four initiator classes produce rc 2 (task-notification, auto-compaction continuation, cross-session peer, and voice-lint's own refusal record), while the discriminating control (an owner-typed record in the same slot) produces rc 0. So the direction is FALSE REFUSAL, which is today's behaviour, and this is a coverage limit rather than a regression: the fix does not help in those turns and does not make them worse. That is the opposite direction from everything my round-1 veto was about, and a security control whose residual fails loud is the kind that may ship. The spec is also right to bound it to the window between a status write and the next owner-typed message, and right to label the 37.4%/62.6% episode figures a POPULATION and not a false-refusal rate, with the reason (no status.json history to join against) stated. Giving this up is what closes AC13, so it is a deliberate trade and the spec books both sides of it now.

THE NESTING FIX IS REAL AND AC8(f) ACTUALLY CATCHES IT, VERIFIED BY IMPLEMENTING THE MISREADING. origin is record-level: 2,746 record-level origin objects and ZERO under message across 1,824 files / 399,019 records (BA: 2,742 / 1,817 / 398,088; the delta is this session's own records). Both halves move in opposite directions, which is the signature the pair exists to produce and which a single cell could not give. R5's warning is also correct that AC14 cannot see this: a predicate that finds no human turn anywhere is permanently loud, and loud is what every drift cell asserts, so the whole drift battery passes trivially while the control is a total silent no-op. AC8(f) plus the new requirement that the OWNER control record be captured rather than hand-written (which stops an implementation's nesting error and a fixture's nesting error cancelling) is the right pair of measures. This was not on my round-2 list and DBA was right to raise it.

SCOPE NOTE ON TWO NUMBERS THAT LOOK LIKE THEY CONTRADICT MY ROUND-2 CENSUS AND DO NOT. AC8 cites '0 of 28,992 user records carry isSidechain true' and '28,992 of 28,992 carry message.role === user'. I reproduce both over MAIN-session transcripts: 0 of 29,067 and 29,067 of 29,067. It should be named in the header so the enum does not read as closed.
